title: Running Email AI on Local Models: What You Control and What It Costs
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: A self-hosted email app does not automatically mean self-hosted inference. Laravel Mail includes Ollama provider support, but the configured endpoint decides where prompts go. A model on another server is still a network service, even when you operate both machines.
content:
Start with the endpoint

A self-hosted email app does not automatically mean self-hosted inference. Laravel Mail includes Ollama provider support, but the configured endpoint decides where prompts go. A model on another server is still a network service, even when you operate both machines.

Benchmark the work you actually do

Start with subject-line drafts or structured classifications on a small test set. Check correctness, latency and failure handling before using the model on a live campaign. Model size alone is not a promise of acceptable output.

Count the full cost

Local inference can avoid a hosted provider's per-token charge. It still consumes hardware, memory, electricity and maintenance time. Extra concurrency increases memory demand; queue limits and timeouts matter just as they do for an email worker.

Keep cloud fallback explicit

Ollama supports cloud-hosted models as well as local ones. Its documentation describes a local-only mode. Choose deliberately, test which endpoint receives requests, and do not silently send subscriber details to a cloud service when a local request fails.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
